plan.contextChunk: This figure places two space-filling molecular models side by side on a white ground, labeled "(a)" and "(b)" in small type beneath them. In model (a), two large green spheres each labeled "Cl" sit at the upper left and upper right, and a single red sphere labeled "O" is wedged between them and forward, sitting lower, so the three atoms describe a shallow V with the oxygen at the vertex. The spheres carry soft highlights and interpenetrate where the atoms are bonded, giving the fused outline of a space-filling representation rather than balls joined by sticks. Model (b) reverses the pattern: one large green sphere labeled "Cl" occupies the lower center and two red spheres labeled "O" rise from it at the upper left and upper right, again bent, this time with chlorine at the vertex. The red oxygens are noticeably smaller than the green chlorines, reflecting relative atomic size. Drawing both at one scale in one style asks the reader to compare which atom sits at the center and how many of each kind surround it. The pair are dichlorine monoxide and chlorine dioxide, the chlorine oxides used commercially for bleaching pulp and flour and for treating water.

interactionPlan.geometry_notes: Use a front-facing, textbook-like space-filling molecular rendering on a white background. Treat +X as screen-right, +Y as screen-up, and +Z as toward the viewer so the central/front atom partially covers the two rear atoms. Overall scene spans roughly X=-4.2 to +4.2, Y=-1.8 to +1.6, Z=-1 to +1. For Cl2O panel (a), molecule center near X=-2.1, Y=0.15. Chlorine radius about 0.92 world units, oxygen radius about 0.70 world units. Place Cl2O oxygen at local coordinates (0, -0.28, +0.38), left Cl at (-0.72, 0.42, -0.12), right Cl at (+0.72, 0.42, -0.12). This makes the green Cl spheres form the upper left and upper right lobes and the red O sphere form the lower central forward lobe, overlapping both chlorines. For ClO2 panel (b), molecule center near X=+2.1, Y=0.15. Place central Cl at local coordinates (0, -0.25, +0.36), left O at (-0.70, 0.52, -0.10), right O at (+0.70, 0.52, -0.10). This makes the green Cl sphere occupy the lower central foreground and the two red O spheres occupy upper left and upper right. Cl2O label '(a)' at about (-2.1, -1.45); ClO2 label '(b)' at about (+2.1, -1.45). Colors: chlorine green gradient base #38c947 with darker lower rim #078949 and pale highlight #9ee87b; oxygen red gradient base #ef2028 with darker lower rim #8d1016 and pale highlight #ff7777. Element text: 'Cl' black #000000, bold sans-serif, centered on visible sphere faces; 'O' white #ffffff, bold sans-serif. In focus toggle, focused molecule should scale to about 1.12 and opacity 1.0; unfocused molecule should scale to about 0.82 and opacity about 0.28 to preserve comparison without competing for attention. Keep both panels in their left/right positions so the source layout remains recognizable.
interactionPlan.notes: Render atoms as high-segment SphereGeometry with Phong or Standard material, strong ambient plus one area/key light from upper left to reproduce soft highlights. Allow sphere interpenetration; do not draw bonds or sticks. Use depth sorting so the central atom in each molecule appears in front of the two surrounding atoms. Text labels should be billboards or CSS2D labels locked to the camera-facing sphere surfaces. The click interaction should only respond to the central atom of the currently focused molecule; when clicked, add a bright outline or semi-transparent halo to the central atom and both attached atoms, plus optional short subtle arcs between their centers to emphasize the V without changing the space-filling style.

authoredContext:
As a class, the oxides are extremely reactive and unstable, and their chemistry has little practical importance. Dichlorine oxide, formally called dichlorine monoxide, and chlorine dioxide, both shown in the figure, are the only commercially important compounds. They are important as bleaching agents (for use with pulp and flour) and for water treatment.

This image shows the structures of the (a) Cl2O and (b) ClO2 molecules.

Two space filling models are shown and labeled, “a,” and “b.” Model a shows a red atom labeled, “O,” bonded to two green atoms labeled, “C l,” in a v-shape. Model b shows a green atom labeled, “C l,” bonded to two red atoms labeled, “O,” in a v-shape.
